claims.text: The starting W–Cu composite exhibits phase separation and interfacial voids.
Adding a low level of a Ni-containing additive and applying transient liquid-phase sintering will suppress phase separation in W–Cu.
The Ni-assisted treatment will suppress interfacial void formation in W–Cu.
A heat-treatment temperature above the melting point of Ni but below that of Cu can create the proposed transient liquid phase while preserving the Cu matrix.
The treatment will form a thin, Ni-rich, continuous binder layer at W–Cu interfaces.
The Ni-derived transient liquid will wet both tungsten and copper.
Wetting by the transient liquid will fill existing interfacial voids.
Wetting and liquid-phase redistribution will mitigate phase separation in the W–Cu composite.
After solidification, the Ni-rich layer will maintain a robust, coherent W–Cu interface.
The Ni-rich interfacial layer will reduce thermal boundary resistance.
The Ni-rich interface will provide structural stability under thermal and irradiation stresses.
Ni-treated W–Cu will have lower interfacial void density than untreated W–Cu after comparable service-relevant exposure.
Ni-treated W–Cu will exhibit less phase separation than untreated W–Cu after comparable service-relevant exposure.
Ni-treated W–Cu will have higher thermal conductivity than untreated W–Cu under high-heat-flux and irradiation conditions.
Phase segregation and interfacial void formation limit the thermal conductivity of untreated W–Cu under service conditions.
The approach is expected to be effective when the Ni-containing additive is limited to a few volume percent.
The Ni-rich interphase may develop new phase instabilities during extended irradiation and thermal cycling.

contradictions.description: The specified processing window is internally infeasible: elemental Ni has a higher melting point than Cu, so a temperature cannot simultaneously be above the melting point of Ni and below that of Cu. This conflicts with the requirement to activate a Ni liquid while preserving the Cu matrix.
